title: What is known about 1RB0LA_1RC---_1RD1RA_1LE1RF_1LC1LE_0RC0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_1RC---_1RD1RA_1LE1RF_1LC1LE_0RC0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. Its run looks like the separator counters of this group: a block of 1s at the right end grows by 4 cells per visit of the head while the time per visit doubles, and the blocks to its left change slowly. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The clock is proved in Lean for every size (tick): what remains is the word map P, one excursion of the head into the blocks left of the counter, iterated 2j times by tick j. The machine can only halt inside an excursion (B reading a 1 in a long block, from a closed tape language computed outside Lean); no invariant of the words that excludes it is known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 244 cells have been visited and 122 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text: A, B, C, D and F cross runs of the words 001, 100 or 11 rightwards in one state, rewriting each copy the same way, for any number of copies and any surrounding tape.

claims.title: No halt in 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator runs 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps without a halt.

claims.title: Events
claims.text: At the visits of F to the right end on blank the tape is blocks of 1s split by single 0s, 1^2 0 1^x … 0 1^N F>0, with x in {1, 5, 9, 13} except a few blocks near the start of a phase; within a phase N grows by 4 per event and the time between events doubles. Phases end with a rebuild: at step 2,114,623 (N 61 to 6) and at step 2,736,109,137 (N 106 to 2); after the second a block of 41 stands before N.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: A closed tape language with windows of 6 cells (found and checked by bbtools.ctl, not yet in Lean) allows a halt only with B reading a 1 and six 1s on its left: inside a long block of 1s.

claims.title: The clock: tick j is 2^j excursions
claims.text: On the mirror image (L and R swapped), write J j W for the tape 1^(5+4j) 0 W from the head. If W goes to W' by 2j excursions (PChain: each one takes L 1 E> W to L F> 1 W' for every L) of total cost E, then 0^4 D> J j W reaches D> J (j+1) W' in exactly E + 51·2j − 4 steps, for every j and every tape beyond the four 0s. The block is a binary counter with digits 1000/0000; the proof is an induction on j (cnt) over three rules proved for all sizes (sweep, increment, finish). The statement is conditional on the excursions returning.

claims.title: The mirror image runs like the machine
claims.text: Every run of the mirror machine is, mirrored, a run of the machine (of_mirror, from a one-step lemma for any pair of mirrored tables), so the tick holds for the machine itself at the right end of its tape.

claims.title: The clock carries the run from blank tape
claims.text: The run of the mirror image from blank tape is at D> J 0 W at step 9,321; the 15 excursions of the next four ticks are each proved for every tape to the left, and the tick theorem (levels 0 to 3; 56, 132, 276 and 532 steps) takes the run to D> J 4 W' at step 10,317. So the hypothesis of the tick is met by the real run: the theorem is not vacuous.

claims.title: The accelerated simulator agrees with the direct run
claims.text: A simulator that does every tick whose excursions all return at once (word after 2j applications of P, the step count of the theorem) agrees with tmrun at all 54 visits of the end in the first 109 steps (time, block length, word).

claims.title: The word map
claims.text: What one excursion does to the blocks left of the counter as arithmetic, what a rebuild (an excursion that does not return to the counter) does, and whether an excursion can reach the halting context B on 1. An invariant of the words closed under P and under the rebuilds would decide the machine.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC1LE_1RA1LD_0LB0LC_1LF0RE_1LB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RE_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_0RA0RB_1RF0LE_1RA--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. The last block of 1s is a binary counter with 4-cell digits: the tick that lengthens it by 4 cells sends the head 2^j times into the rest of the tape, and each visit applies the same word map. That clock is proved in Lean for every size; what the word map does in the long run is the open part.

facts.text: Tick j of the clock, proved for every j (given that the excursions return).
Its exact step count, E the cost of the excursions.
No halt in the C simulator.
The only place a halt can happen (closed tape language).

sections.heading: Visits to the right end
html: Call it an event when the head arrives at the right end of the tape in state F, on blank. At events the tape is blocks of 1s split by single 0s and the last block is long; the earlier blocks have 1, 5, 9 or 13 ones. Within a phase the last block grows by 4 per event and each event takes about twice as long as the previous one (run of 3·109 steps):
Over these events the blocks on the left do not change except at the end next to N; doubling time means the last block is a binary counter that counts up to about 2N/4 between events.

sections.heading: The clock
html: Mirror the machine (swap left and right), so that the growing block is at the left end. Whenever the head is at the left end the tape is D> 1^(5+4j) 0 W: a block, a 0, and a word W. One tick eats four blank cells and makes the block four longer. Inside a tick:

partwhat happenssteps
sweep0^4 D> 1^(5+4j) 0 becomes 0 1 1 0 0 0 (0000)^j 1 1 1 1 E>: the block is turned into a counter at zero4j + 20
excursion1 E> W comes back as F> 1 W': one application of the word map Pdepends on W
increment0000 (1000)^n 1 1 1 F> 1 becomes 1000 (0000)^n 1 1 1 1 E>: add one, go back into the word18n + 33
finishwith the counter full, 0 1 1 0 0 0 (1000)^j 1 1 1 F> 1 becomes D> 1^(9+4j) 014j + 27

The counter has j digits, so the head makes 2j excursions before the finish: the word after the tick is P applied 2j times, and the tick takes E + 51·2j − 4 steps, E being the cost of the excursions. Lean proves this for every j by induction (the low j digits count through twice, with one increment of the digit above in between), and the same file follows the run from blank tape through four ticks (steps 9,321 to 10,317 of the mirror image), so the theorem does apply to the real run.

The theorem is conditional: it assumes each excursion returns to the counter. A phase ends with an excursion that does not (the rebuilds below), and a halt, if there is one, happens inside an excursion. So everything about halting is now a question about the word map P.

sections.heading: Rebuilds
html: A phase ends when the counter's carry reaches the blocks on the left in a certain way: the tape is rebuilt and N starts again from a few cells.

stepN beforeN after
2,114,623616
2,736,109,1371062
Before step 2,114,623 the phases were short (N reaching 5 to 57). The phase that started at step 2,736,109,137 has 67 blocks on its left, and N had reached 90 at step 2,878,809,076.

sections.heading: Sweeps
html: The head moves through the tape crossing repeated words in one state, rewriting each copy the same way: for example A turning 0 0 1 into 1 1 1, or D turning 1 1 into 1 0. These rules are proved in Lean for any number of copies: a_right_001, b_right_001, c_right_100, d_right_11, d_right_100, f_right_11, f_right_001.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The machine halts only when B reads a 1. A closed tape language with windows of six cells (an over-approximation of the configurations reachable from blank tape, found by bbtools.ctl) allows that only with six 1s on B's left, inside a long block. The same is true of the separator counters 1RB---_1RC0RD_1RD1RA_1LE1RB_0LF0LE_1RF0RD and 1RB---_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RF0RB_0LF1RA, which halt only when their slow counter is all ones; whether something similar holds here is not known.

sections.heading: Next steps
html: The clock reduces the machine to its word map P (one excursion). Next: write P as arithmetic on the blocks left of the counter (lengths 1, 5, 9, 13), find what the non-returning excursions (rebuilds) do, and look for an invariant of the words closed under both that excludes B reading a 1; the outside Coq proofs of three other clock machines (busycoq PRs 48, 50, 53) show the kind of invariant that works there.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.028).
After 109 steps the tape spans 244 cells (23 left of the start, 216 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RA_1LC1LE_1RA1LD_0LB0LC_1LF0RE_1LB---: rename A→E, B→F, C→B, D→C, E→A, F→D and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state E, in a mirror
  • 1RB1RE_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_0RA0RB_1RF0LE_1RA---: rename A→E, B→F, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→D; it is this table started in state C
  • 1RB---_1RC1RF_1LD1RE_1LB1LD_0RB0RC_1RA0LF: rename A→F, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→E; it is this table started in state B

summary: A clock at the right end: the last block of 1s is a binary counter with 4-cell digits, and the tick that lengthens it from 5+4j to 9+4j cells makes exactly 2^j excursions into the rest of the tape (one word map P per excursion), in E + 51·2^j − 4 steps: proved in Lean for every j, and followed on the run from blank tape for 4 ticks. Whether P always returns is open.
family: clock and word map (block grows by 4, right end)
